ai.description: *Indirana beddomii* reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with a dark lateral band and pale dorsolateral folds. Key features include a pointed snout and long, slender limbs adapted for leaping.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana beddomii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark lateral band extending from the snout through the eye to the flanks, contrasting with its pale, granular belly.
ai.habitat: *Indirana beddomii* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome’s leaping frogs are primarily nocturnal, using their powerful hind legs to perform explosive jumps to escape predators or navigate their forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana beddomii* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 200–400 eggs on moist rocks or leaf litter near streams, where larvae develop semi-terrestrially.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana beddomii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting moist forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Indirana beddomii* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps typically heard near rocky streams in rainforest habitats.
